entries.label: Amazon Web Services (AWS) credential
entries.whyItMatters: Trawl found the following in a public code repository, where anyone can read it: {{secretType}}. Repositories are copied, cached and searched by others, so a value that has appeared in one has to be treated as known to outsiders.
entries.howItCouldBeAbused: An attacker wants to use your cloud account: to run their own computing at your expense, to read or take stored data, or to change or delete your systems. The consequence for the organization is a data breach, an outage and unexpected charges.
entries.whatGoodLooksLike: Good looks like no secrets in code at all. Secrets are held in a managed store, credentials are short-lived, and a check blocks them before they are published.
whatToDo: Ask the cloud account owner to deactivate and replace the credential now, before doing anything else.
Review the activity records for the credential from the date it was first published, and look for any use you do not recognize.
Remove the value from the current code and load it from a secret store instead.
Remember that removing it from the latest version does not remove it from the repository's history or from copies others have made. Revoking it is what ends the risk.
Add a check to the publishing process that blocks secrets before they are committed.
entries.howRescanConfirms: The next scan reads the repository again. The finding closes when the value no longer appears in the current files. A scan reads only the latest version, so only revoking the credential confirms that the risk has ended. If a later scan cannot complete this check, the finding stays open and is marked as not re-assessed.
